record.file_problem: The README is cut off at 60,000 characters and ends mid-table; repo contents were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and capability outcomes for a mean-direction-based weight-edit abliteration, testing practical removal rather than the original residual-stream intervention.
record.gate_note: The README reports results for this repository's own Qwen3.6-27B release and abliteration trials. Its discussion of other papers' results is not recorded as study results. Serving-throughput benchmarks do not measure the claim's refusal-direction behavior and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The README applies a mean-difference weight-edit abliteration to a released hybrid-attention model, Qwen3.6-27B. It reports refusals on harmful prompts before and after the edit, which bears directly on V2 in a new setting. The method has additions (NPBA projection, winsorization, Optuna search, a prior conv1d repair). It is the authors' own release with self-reported results, not a stated replication.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors present trial 46 as a 'lossless', 'capability-enhanced' uncensored release: 0/100 refusals, 10/10 coherent spot-checks and very low KL. They warn that keyword refusal scoring missed the incoherence of the more aggressive trial 17. The capability-enhancement claim rests on cited literature and arguments, not on the authors' own benchmark measurements.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a harmful/harmless mean-vector method, but implements abliteration through weight edits and combines orthogonal projection, projected abliteration, winsorization, per-layer scope, and an optimization search rather than testing residual-stream projection at every layer and position. This is a tool/release repository, not a stated replication.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports different capability outcomes for trial 17 and trial 46; trial 46 uses per-layer vector scope and gentler weight limits than trial 17.

fits_no_version.finding: The released model has a first-3-token KL of 0.000492 against the base. Trial 17 had KL 0.00192 yet was incoherent, so low KL did not guarantee coherence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Low KL divergence against the base does not by itself indicate preserved capability after abliteration.

record.problems: Results are self-reported in the README and the code was not run. The harmful-prompt evaluation has 100 prompts, and capability evidence is a 10-axis spot-check. The README notes that keyword-only refusal scoring missed the incoherence in trial 17.
record.rows_left_out: No other claim-relevant outcome rows were identified in the provided README text. The file list names benchmark results, but their contents were not available for inspection.

untested.parts: Only one model was tested, and there is no independent replication. The refusal scoring method is not stated, and there is no judge-based or held-out harmful set. Capability was not measured on standard benchmarks. The README's 'capability-enhanced' claims rest on cited literature, not on its own measurements.
There is no residual-stream ablation or refusal-inducing addition.
Qwen3.6 has a thinking mode, but refusal-direction behaviour during reasoning is not examined separately.

missing.what: Output length deviation against the base: 0.027 σ for the released model.
KL against the base per trial: trial 17 at 0.00192, trial 46 at 0.00049, with their edit parameters.
Confound: before abliteration, Stage 1 rescaled 8 SSM conv1d blocks (layers 52–62), so the refusal comparison is not abliteration alone.

record.verdict_notes: This is a self-promotional model-release README, truncated at 60k characters, and most of it covers serving throughput, which is irrelevant to the claim. All results are self-reported, with a single run, no uncertainty, and no stated refusal scorer. The text contains no instructions directed at the reader. Tranche set to T3 rather than T2: the method is close to standard abliteration (V2's own method), applied to a new hybrid-attention model.

versions.untested_parts: No residual-stream ablation at every layer and position, refusal-inducing addition, or direct test of the specified causal intervention.
Only this Qwen3.6-27B release is reported; other released models and independent replication are not tested.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or training against its ablation.
No test comparing a single direction with an affine, cone, or multiple-direction account.
No separate measurement of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, model-variant, or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal-training methods or timing.
No test of reasoning-model refusal-direction behavior.

relation.reason: The README reports its own refusal counts for the base and the edited model (99/100 to 0/100), plus a capability check.

tranche.reason: It applies a mean-difference weight-edit abliteration to a new hybrid-attention/GatedDeltaNet model and reports refusals before and after. T2 is also defensible because of the NPBA, winsorization and Optuna additions, but the new architecture is the main new element.

source_check.notes: The record's authors_conclusion is accurate: the capability-enhancement claim rests on cited literature, not on the authors' own benchmarks. The release also includes a Stage 1 conv1d rescaling of 8 SSM blocks before abliteration. The KL is first-3-token KL. No refusal test is reported separately for the NVFP4 variants. The README is cut at 60,000 characters, but only in the Troubleshooting section, which doesn't matter here.

statements.problem: What it says about this study is right: Qwen3.6-27B is a hybrid (16 full-attention + 48 GatedDeltaNet layers), and conv1d rescaling ran before abliteration. The study id is shortened to gh:aeon-7/qwen3.6-27b.

statements.correction: Trial 17: global vector_scope, o_proj max_weight 2.50, down_proj max_weight 5.43, KL 0.00192, 0/100 keyword refusals, smoke test BROKEN (gibberish). Trial 46: per-layer scope, 1.56 / 3.45, KL 0.00049, 0/100 refusals, COHERENT. The guard was a post-hoc 10-axis capability spot-check, not a regularizer in the optimizer.
statements.problem: The 0/100 keyword refusals and gibberish for trial 17 are right. But 'the lowest-refusal trial' and 'trial 17' are the same trial, and the released trial 46 also reached 0/100, so the refusal count was not what separated them. The difference was edit scope and strength.
